title: The Hermit Tarot Card Meaning: Upright, Reversed & Love
description: The Hermit upright: solitude, reflection, inner guidance; reversed: isolation or no quiet. Love, work, advice and Waite's 1911 text. Ask your question.
image_alt: The Hermit, 1909 Rider–Waite–Smith card: a gray-bearded old man in a long gray hooded cloak holds up a glowing lantern and leans on a tall yellow staff, standing on a white peak.
capsule: The Hermit is card IX of the Major Arcana: solitude, soul-searching, reflection and the wisdom you find once the noise drops away. Reversed, solitude sours into isolation and loneliness, or busyness crowds quiet out. It is a calm card asking for time. Not clear yet is the honest yes-or-no answer: his light reaches only a few steps ahead.

blocks.heading: What is on The Hermit card?
paragraphs: An old man with a long gray beard stands alone on a white, jagged peak, wrapped in a gray hooded cloak that reaches the ground. He holds a lantern up in his right hand and grips a tall yellow staff with his left, eyes lowered. Waite writes that "it is a star which shines in the lantern" and that the figure is "holding up his beacon on an eminence" (p. 104).
His robed figure fills almost the whole height of the 1909 card. The lantern gives a yellow glow with short rays around it, the sky behind him is a pale blue-gray, and IX appears above his hood.

His beacon, Waite says, intimates "where I am, you also may be" (p. 104). Earlier in the book he calls this "a card of attainment" rather than "a card of quest" (p. 17), and lists other names for the figure: the Capuchin and, in more philosophical language, the Sage (p. 16).

blocks.heading: What did Waite write about The Hermit?
paragraphs: Waite's upright list opens with prudence and circumspection, good judgment and care, then turns to several kinds of deceit. The reversed list is about hiding and holding back: concealment, disguise, fear, caution with no good reason behind it.

In his own reading the lamp counts for more than the hiding. He saw a counsel of prudence in the Hermit "pursuing a solitary path by the light of his own lamp" (p. 22), and he rejected linking the card with "occult isolation", a closed-off kind of self-protection (p. 104).

blocks.heading: What does The Hermit mean upright?
paragraphs: The Hermit upright is about solitude chosen on purpose: stepping back from the noise so you can hear your own answers. Its common modern meaning is soul-searching and introspection, a stretch of time alone looking for what is true for you, sometimes a spiritual search. The card turns up when outside advice has stopped helping and you need time to think before you choose.
The lantern is the heart of it. It shows only the ground just ahead, and that is enough to walk by. Reflection here is practical: one question held long enough for inner guidance to come through.
Wisdom in this card is earned slowly and shared quietly. Time alone with yourself is not loneliness here but focus. One question to carry with you: what do I need some quiet to hear clearly?

blocks.heading: What does The Hermit mean reversed?
paragraphs: Reversed, The Hermit means isolation and loneliness: a withdrawal that began as rest and turned into a wall, or a sense of being cut off from others. Or the opposite, constant busyness, avoiding quiet so that reflection never gets a turn.
Waite's reversed words, concealment, disguise and fear, describe the first case: pulling back and keeping hidden. The second, a life too full for silence, is a modern reading, not Waite's.
Both leave you without a clear inner signal. Ask whether you need more quiet or more company right now, and give yourself a little of whichever is missing.

blocks.heading: What does The Hermit mean in love?
paragraphs: A lamp held up to your own heart comes before any sharing: that is The Hermit's way in love. In a relationship it often means a phase of distance: needing space, a quieter season, room to think before talking things over. Needing space is not the same as pulling away.
Unpartnered, the card often describes a period of being single by choice, time spent getting to know yourself, so that what you look for in someone comes from a clearer place.

With the lantern turned upside down, it can mean loneliness in love, or emotional distance that has gone on too long between two people. Notice whether solitude has become a hiding place, or whether you stay so busy with others that you never check in with yourself. What do you know about your own wishes that you have not said aloud?

blocks.heading: What does The Hermit mean for work and money?
paragraphs: Money choices go better in slow light. The card's money meaning is frugal and careful: spending less, thinking long-term, valuing meaning over things. Do you allow yourself room to think before you decide, or let noise and comparison push you along?

Deep, focused work and time to think things through are where this card shines on the job: research, study, a plan made slowly. It may also suggest looking for a mentor with more experience, or becoming that guide for someone else.
In its reversed form, check whether you have cut yourself off from people who could help, with work or with money, or are too busy to step back and see the whole picture.

blocks.heading: What is The Hermit's advice?
paragraphs: Take a walk alone and carry one open question with you, without rushing to answer it. Protect a small pocket of quiet in your day and listen to whatever surfaces there.

blocks.heading: Is The Hermit a yes or no card?
The Hermit as a person and as feelings
paragraphs: A mentor, a quiet thinker, someone who keeps a little apart and sees clearly because of it: these are the people The Hermit tends to describe, and read as you, it marks the quiet part of yourself that knows more than it says. Emotionally, the card is traditionally slow and inward: real affection kept private, a need for space and time to think before anything is said, a heart that is reserved and careful rather than cold. Reversed, those feelings close further, into emotional distance, withdrawal and loneliness, or turn into a restlessness that cannot sit still.

pairs.text: Inner knowing beside reflection. Trust the quiet answer you can already half hear.
Two calls to step back at once. Real rest is the task, not a delay.
Stillness, then movement. Let the time apart set a direction before you push forward.
A pause to take stock. Look at what has grown before you decide what to tend next.

blocks.heading: The Hermit or the Eight of Cups?
paragraphs: Both cards show a lone figure apart from others. In the Eight of Cups, "a man of dejected aspect is deserting the cups" of his past efforts (p. 210); the modern reading is walking away to search for meaning. The Hermit is further along: Waite set him on a height with his beacon raised (p. 104). The Eight is about leaving something behind; The Hermit, about the quiet you find once you stop and look inward.

blocks.heading: Questions to ask yourself about The Hermit
paragraphs: What question keeps coming back when things get quiet?
Where do I need more silence, and where more company?
What do I already know that I have been too busy to hear?

faq.q: Is The Hermit a good or bad card?
faq.a: It is a thoughtful card more than a good or bad one. Rest, stillness and finding answers of your own are what it supports. The one risk is staying withdrawn after the quiet has done its work: time alone is meant to end with a clearer step back toward people.

faq.q: Does The Hermit mean being lonely?
faq.a: No. It describes solitude you choose, not loneliness forced on you. Waite saw the figure as someone who has already reached a height and raises a light others can follow (pp. 17, 104). If loneliness is what you feel, the reversed side comes closer: a silence that has lasted longer than it helps.

faq.q: What is inside The Hermit's lantern?
faq.a: A star, in Waite's words (p. 104). His only change to the older design concerned the light: "the lamp is not enveloped partially in the mantle of its bearer" (p. 104). Earlier commentators said the lantern held "the Light of Occult Science" (p. 17), a reading Waite felt missed the higher side of the card.

faq.q: Does The Hermit tell me to cut people off?
faq.a: Not as a rule. Its quiet is meant to send you back with something clearer to share, and the reversed side already marks a retreat that has gone on too long. Stepping back for a while and closing a door for good are different choices; the card asks only for the first.

waite.quote: Prudence, circumspection; also and especially treason, dissimulation, roguery, corruption. Reversed: Concealment, disguise, policy, fear, unreasoned caution.
